pages.texte:
Zeffy
Zeffy empowers nonprofits with free and efficient fundraising, so they can focus on supporting their communities.

Zeffy has enabled thousands of charities across Canada to raise millions of dollars in online donations, run fundraising campaigns and manage their event box office at no cost. The platform allows them to increase their social impact by raising more funds thanks to an innovative remuneration model based on voluntary contributions and its intuitive interface.

FOUNDER.S
Thibaut Jaurou & François de Kerret
LOCATED
Montreal, CAN
WEBSITE
Zeffy
FUND
Mission
SOCIALS
THE CHALLENGE
THEY WANT TO SOLVE

Zeffy's mission is to support Non Profit Organisations which are engaged in many UN SDGs’ fields in their critical (and sometimes costly) process of fundraising.

THE IMPACT
THEY HAVE

Zeffy offers to Non Profit Organisations an efficient and costless fundraising suite, thus enabling them to increase their reach, onboard and better engage donors while saving the funds raised to fund their operations rather than pay fees.

THE WAY
WE MEASURE IT

We measure both the number of charities onboarded as well as the amount raised through the platform.

ISAAC
Protect your structure with the first patented active protection system featuring Active Mass Damper technology.

 ISAAC is a deep tech company developing intelligent, non-invasive seismic solutions for critical infrastructures.

FOUNDER.S
Alberto Bussini
LOCATED
Milan, IT
WEBSITE
ISAAC
FUND
Mission
SOCIALS
THE CHALLENGE
THEY WANT TO SOLVE

ISAAC addresses the structural vulnerability of buildings located in seismic zones, where conventional seismic protection solutions are often costly, complex and intrusive.

THE IMPACT
THEY HAVE

ISAAC enhances building resilience through plug-and-play dampers able to offset seismic shifts or violent vibrations. By simplifying deployment and minimising structural intervention, the company enables broader adoption of seismic protection across sensitive buildings (e.g., schools, hospitals, public buildings).

THE WAY
WE MEASURE IT

We monitor the number of critical infrastructures equipped and the number of underserved zones that are protected.

THEY WANT TO SOLVE
pages.texte:
Lixo
AI-powered waste management solutions reducing sorting errors and optimising recycling efficiency.

Lixo provides AI-powered tools for waste collection trucks to improve sorting accuracy, enhance recycling and operational efficiency. By combining data analysis with actionable insights, Lixo enables municipalities and operators to reduce contamination, prevent fires, and optimise costs, while fostering sustainable waste management practices.

FOUNDER.S
Marjorie Darcet & Olivier Large
LOCATED
Paris, FR
WEBSITE
Lixo
FUND
Mission
SOCIALS
THE CHALLENGE
THEY WANT TO SOLVE

Waste sorting remains a persistent challenge. Sorting quality issues are a key pain point for waste management operators, who also face regulatory obligations to enhance recycling performance. Significant sorting errors persist, leading to high costs in waste treatment, logistics, insurance, and lost opportunities (estimated at ~€450 per ton). In line with a European Directive, French municipalities are increasingly required to enforce effective waste sorting among residents. In selective collection, 100 tonnes typically include 17-25 tonnes of sorting errors, generating substantial financial losses across the waste value chain.

THE IMPACT
THEY HAVE

Lixo addresses these challenges with an AI-powered solution deployed on waste collection trucks. By the end of 2024, over 55,000 tonnes of waste were analysed monthly. Lixo combines behavioural insights, targeting awareness campaigns in underperforming neighbourhoods, with advanced data analysis to optimise waste streams and recycling capacity. Safety measures reduce sorting errors, CO₂ emissions, and fire risks, while protecting workers by detecting hazardous items. Lixo has demonstrated the ability to reduce sorting errors by up to 50% in highly contaminated areas. For example, addressing errors costing €1.5 million per year can yield a 25% reduction, translating to savings of €375,000 annually.

THE WAY
WE MEASURE IT

We measure the volume of waste analysed (in tons) the evolution of the contamination score (index) and the number of awareness campaigns (per year).

THE CHALLENGE
THEY WANT TO SOLVE
pages.texte:
EverDye
Revolutionising textile dyeing with low-energy, biobased pigments for a greener, safer, and circular process.

Everdye transforms the dyeing stage in the textile and fashion industry, one of the most polluting sectors globally, by using low-heat, low-energy, biobased pigments and sustainable dyeing methods.

FOUNDER.S
Amira Erokh, Philippe Berlan
LOCATED
Paris, FR
WEBSITE
EverDye
FUND
Mission
SOCIALS
THE CHALLENGE
THEY WANT TO SOLVE

The fashion and textile industry contributes to nearly 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions, with more than half arising from dyeing processes, and are responsible for 20% of industrial water pollution. Traditional dyeing exposes workers to toxic chemicals and involves physically arduous work. The sector also lacks circularity, generating significant waste and environmental degradation. EverDye addresses these systemic issues by offering a cleaner, safer, and circular dyeing solution.

THE IMPACT
THEY HAVE

Everdye delivers both environmental and social benefits. Environmentally, it reduces CO₂ emissions, water usage, and chemical consumption, preserves biodiversity, enables zero-waste dyeing, and promotes circularity through recyclable and reusable pigments. Socially, it limits workers’ exposure to toxic substances and reduces the physical strain of traditional dyeing, improving health and working conditions. The solution also offers a scalable, low-cost method that can be implemented across the fashion value chain, redefining sustainability standards.

THE WAY
WE MEASURE IT

Everdye significantly reduces water usage by lowering the litres of water consumed per ton of textile dyed, scaled across annual production volumes. Energy consumption is also minimised, with fewer kWh used per tonne of textile, aggregated over yearly output. Worker safety is improved by eliminating exposure to toxic chemicals in dyeing houses. Industrial validation has been successfully achieved, with scale-up from laboratory tests of 1 ml to industrial batches of 150L, including pilot programmes with international brands that demonstrate both feasibility and performance.
